newsitem.title: INDIA: India permits sugar exports to meet past contracts.
newsitem.headline: India permits sugar exports to meet past contracts.

text.p: India has authorised a fresh export quota of 100,000 tonnes of sugar to avoid defaulting on past contracts to Indonesia, a sugar export agency official said on Wednesday.
The federal government made the decision early in December, an official of the Indian Sugar and General Industries Import Export Corporation (ISIGIEC) told Reuters.
"The government agreed to release it 15 days ago because otherwise we would have defaulted on the contract," said the official, who did not want to be identified.
The official said the 100,000 tonnes of sugar were meant for Indonesia.
The agency had asked the government to release the quota to meet previous contracts three months ago, he added.
The Business Line newspaper said on Wednesday that the government had allowed ISIGIEC to export the 100,000 tonnes of sugar in addition to an earlier allocation of 125,000 tonnes.
But it did not state the export period.
The ISIGIEC official said the agency had already shipped the earlier allocation of 125,000 tonnes to Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Indonesia and elsewhere.
He said the agency, set up by private millers, planned to ask the federal government for an additional allocation of at least 50,000 tonnes of sugar.
"We will ask the government for fresh allotment because Pakistan is coming up with a tender on Thursday for the import of 50,000 tonnes of sugar," he said.
"We will be a major player in the market," the official said.

India produced 16.45 million tonnes of sugar in 1995/96 (October-September) against 14.6 million the previous season, industry sources said. India had 5.5 million tonnes of surplus sugar when the season began on October 1 this year.
